purpose: Human-readable mathematical statements for curated benchmarks. These guide reader orientation and do not replace the checked Lean declaration.

fermat-prime-two-squares.statement: If p is prime and p ≡ 1 (mod 4), then p = a² + b² for some integers a and b.

cosine-addition.statement: cos(x + y) = cos x cos y − sin x sin y.

sine-addition.statement: sin(x + y) = sin x cos y + cos x sin y.

cosine-subtraction.statement: cos(x − y) = cos x cos y + sin x sin y.

sine-subtraction.statement: sin(x − y) = sin x cos y − cos x sin y.

quadratic-polynomial-derivative.statement: For f(x) = x², f′(x) = 2x; this benchmark uses an exact finite rational polynomial evaluator.

cubic-polynomial-derivative.statement: For f(x) = x³, f′(x) = 3x²; this benchmark uses an exact finite rational polynomial evaluator.

derivative-uniqueness.statement: At an accumulation point, if a function has two derivatives (within the same set), then those derivative values are equal.

irrational-sqrt-rational.statement: For a nonnegative rational q, √q is irrational exactly when q is not a square of a rational number.

effective-fundamental-theorem-of-calculu.statement: Under the usual hypotheses, ∫ₐᵇ f′(x) dx = f(b) − f(a).

telescoping-reciprocal-series.statement: The reciprocal triangular series sums to 2: Σₙ≥1 1/(n(n+1)/2) = 2.

sine-alternating-taylor-bridge.statement: The certified alternating-series interval for sin agrees with the corresponding Taylor partial-sum interval.

finite-de-moivre-rational-circle.statement: On rational points of the unit circle, taking an n-th power is the same as repeated circle multiplication: a finite geometric De Moivre theorem.

computable-forty-five-unit-circle.statement: The certified computable values of sin(π/4) and cos(π/4) satisfy sin²(π/4) + cos²(π/4) = 1.

finite-rotation-euler-ode-bridge.statement: A finite constant-coefficient rotation ODE expansion agrees exactly with the alternating sine–cosine matrix polynomial from the exponential route.

four-point-parseval.statement: For the unnormalised four-point Fourier transform, the transformed energy is four times the original energy.

pi-circle-area-geometric-arctangent.statement: The circle-area construction of π agrees with four geometric arctangent sectors.

nilakantha-leibniz-pi.statement: The Nilakantha and Leibniz alternating-series algorithms converge to the same value π.
